Raa: He may not roar like a lion but he definitely cackles, usually at the back of the room in the shadows where he cant be seen and so won't get into trouble. He's crashed a lot of cars.
Rabbit: Picture Annie, in a male body. Though not anywhere near as imaginative a lover.
Raechacha: The name of a South Pacific Island dance. You can only do it properly if you are smiling ridiculously, fitter than a Malley Bull, dressed in a islander grass skirt and wielding a spear with the full intention of slaying any bastard who has anything bad to say about you, which obviously never happens.
Rafael: Sure, he's a dreamer, a painter, philosopher, boozer and more, but it's all a front. Rafael knows about life and he knows that all any of us are, really, is some kind of wild, fantastic 3-dimensional video creature in the middle of the most crazy game in the universe. My advice? Do what he does.....
Raff: The scruffy knockabout that women tend to adore. But, he needs to do something about this debt…
Rafferty: Rafferty lives his life as if he's the star of a movie that is running 24/7. It's actually worth watching about 20% of the time.
Rafi:
Great friends with Alby, Rafi has broken or lost so many items that didn't belong to him, it isn't funny. Did he replace them? 
Well, time is short, you see, he never seems to have much cash on him and, well, he always meant it when he said he was going to. On the up side, Rafi wouldn’t hurt a fly.
Ragan: This boy makes clinical decisions, which partially explains his success, but he's a bit too organised.
Raiden: Raiden is a fine fellow but we feel it's premature to be talking about him, here. What isn't finished here Raiden? What have you yet to do or yet to understand? What are you waiting for? Come on, do it. Then we'll talk…
Rain: Mmm, I wonder how the world would treat him if he'd been called Gentle Drizzle. Anyway, Rain broods, at least, he looks like he's brooding. Which means he's probably just not masturbating enough. (I know, hard to imagine, eh?)
Rainer: Rainer smokes only Camel and despite his friends, which are many, his only true allegience is to the Mafia Don who he is entrusted to protect.
Raj: Raj is many things, and the boy sports an ego, but he is definitely loved, although usually by men more so than women. His parents probably hail from the subcontinent but it matters not. Many women rate him as a 'player' at all the nightclubs around town but he'll settle down in the end. Rarely poverty stricken.
Raja: Raja is more humble than his brother, Raj, despite having a healthy sense of self-worth, also. Raja's moral standards appear to be set pretty high and he'd make a fine doctor, although we'd hope the reasons he'd choose such a life path were not solely to please his parents and attract a satisfactory reproductive mate.
Rakhal: His name catches everyone completely off guard and they have no choice but to stand up straight and listen to him, out of surprise as much as anything. The wash-up is that Rakhal is a sufficiently unconventional and honourable man.
Ralph: Ralph is an affable fellow who remembers most jokes, and this says everything about his intellect that is huge. If he had an edge to him he could do anything and exalt in the greatness of his achievements, but then he wouldn’t be Ralph.
Ramey: Like Richie not long after him, Ramey makes a splendid 2nd in charge, or maybe even a 3rd or 4th. Responsibility: who needs that shit, is what might well turn out to be his mantra. But, someone has to make the others laugh and feel comfortable and not everyone can pull it off. There are too many people taking too much of life too seriously anyway. Girls tend to love him, although they're never sure if he's up to this fathering caper. I guess we'll have to wait and see. A funny guy though and a cool cat, so long as no one makes him Captain.
Ramish: Ramish can sit down, close his eyes and inside 30 seconds put himself into a meditative state that brings him straight into his third eye. Sounds wild, eh? And it is. But in here he is granted visions of worlds so splendid we can't describe them. Like a few others out there, he sees the future, he sees the past, and he should probably surf if he doesn’t. It's an energy thing.
Ranald: Plenty of books in his study point to an informed, travelled and rather predictable life. Yes, yes, he’s seen the pyramids and boated down the Mekong but beyond children he’s sticking to the game plan, not that there’s anything wrong with that. If no one paid their taxes roads wouldn’t exist, and then what?
Randal: Randal is a brand new chemistry textbook that ends up spending years in the library, and where he gathers dust and meditates.
Randall: Very similar to Randal, except this textbook has been in the backpack of a gorgeous English girl who has travelled the world. She stole it.
Randolph: Randolph, the great goose, was born about 40 years too late. Then again, imagine if he wasn’t? As a man of means, Randolph might very well toss it all in one day and go off-grid. Ditch the car. Throw out the TV. Get into gardening. These are the deeds of an eccentric man, not to mention a fine and wise one.
Randy: He’s a unit, alright. Randy is an outgoing bloke who drives a Japanese sports car that has purple neon lights attached to the bottom of it and a souped-up muffler attached at the rear. The muffler is big and silver and, secretly, Randy wants a cock that looks and sounds the same.
Ranjeet: Upbeat and savvy, Ranjeet runs an efficient business. He knows many of the family members of most of his employees and this personal touch lends itself to a happy, fun environment. His own family life isn’t too different, although he does love his sons slightly more than his daughters.
Raoul: Raoul is having too much fun to consider doing something as banal as getting a job. But, he's a great dancer, the girls love him and he's rarely rich.
Rasta: Yep, in a past life he was one so what do you do? You remain centred and you fill your life with as much clean fun as is feasible with only 24 hours in a day, and perhaps that’s Rasta’s little secret. Time is a relative concept and if you want it to, it doesn’t even have to exist. Bravo Rasta.
Rastus:
(The lawyer talking to him in the lockup…)

Rastus, I don’t get it. You threw away a mining job of 300 grand a year to come and live in the city. You’re I.Q, according to this testing here, is in the top 1.5% of the population.
(Rastus smiles, shrugs his shoulders.)
So answer me this will you, for someone so smart why do you end up in here so often?
(Rastus looks down at his feet, looks back to his lawyer.)
…Coz’ I get bored out there. And I’ve got an addictive nature. What can I say?

The end.
Raul: Raul has very strict ideas about family morals and behaviour. (Note: If he was born north of Barcelona, dismiss this name theory, immediately, because he is the exact opposite.)
Ravi: The Magician. He has beautiful white teeth, he smiles 95% of the time and he constantly thrills thousands of people with the dance parties that he puts on.
Ray: Ray was released from prison about a year ago after doing something silly when he was much younger and far stupider. He came to regret that but, nowadays, having won back the love of his kids, he wouldn’t trade any of his history for anything. He hasn’t had time to become an entrepreneur.
Rayden: All his friends spent plenty of time in school detention but somehow he managed to slip passed the edge of all that chaos. Indeed, he is often quite discreet and more diplomatic than you think. How this came to be is anyone's guess. Healthy and active, Rayden rarely attracts lots of attention and no one in the Kingdom is as quick and as stealthy as spotting and pocketing a $50 note someone accidentally dropped.
Raymond: Did you ever read that story as a child, "The Hare and the Raymond"? It's one of our favourites. The underdog keeps going and going, never giving up, and he deserves his victory - he's worked hard. The only tragedy is that by the time he crosses the finish line everyone has gone home. Raymond.
Read: (Pronounced Read, as in, I will now go into my room and read my book.) Speaking of which, Read is well-read too. A tall, placid and splendid individual, in a past life Read was a giant rain forest tree - home to literally billions and millions of little critters whom he felt inexorably spiritually attached to.
Reece: Reece is many things - he is a small splinter beneath a finger nail, he is cocky and ever-so-slightly sleazy, he is a good assassin.
Reed: The Vampire. (ie. Nocturnal, probably quite brilliant, partially psychopathic.)
Reef: Reef, don't drop out of school. I know you're thinking about it. Get past the dip, it'll be worth it in the end. Love, Management.
Reese: Sceptical - you bet. Like a very smart dog who has been dropped off at a dog refuge by his previous owners - let's face it, they were never up to the task of caring for another creature properly - he takes a while to warm to people but once he's in, and he trusts you, then whoa betide any man or animal who comes between him and those he loves.
Reg: Reg is as deaf as a decent sized post. He says, “What?” so often and so loudly at the nursing home that people have stopped talking to him, outright. As a young bloke, however, he sold combine harvesters and raised a nice family.
Regan: A name for the silver screen. Regan is a sufficiently thoughtful and dedicated man but if you ever implied that his name had a feminine aspect to it, he would probably pick you up by the throat with one hand and gently tear your head from your shoulders, with the other.
Regi: Regi is the kind of fellow who, if driving, lost,  through the Italian country-side in a rented car with his girlfriend would go out of his way to find a hitch-hiker who could help them figure out where they are. Big smile. Takes very little seriously.
Reginald: A pompous English explorer who never knew his east from south. He was only able to do the travelling he did, anyway, because his father had some pull with the government but all was for nought, however, because in 1910, while on an expedition into the mountains of New Guinea, he was eaten by a tribe of cannibals. Apparently his meat was crap.
Reid: In a past life Reid was a Spanish Conquistador. Good for the modern world. Bad for earth-loving natives.
Reife: Do you know, for all the bullshit and the run-ins, and the useless attributes, Reife is a hopeless romantic who comes good every time.
Reini: The semi-successful mover and shaker who knows all the bouncers at all the clubs. They, and most of the girls inside, as a matter of fact, love him.
Rem: Rem is utterly reliable, not only for a helping hand but for some sound advice and a smile when needed. He doesn’t take days to make decisions and his whole energy attracts good people. Perhaps we should clone him and drop thousands of him into some of the world’s trouble spots? It couldn’t hurt…
Remo:
“Fuck the nanny state.,” he says often. 
Remo is a passionate man who can fix anything and if he can’t he’ll know someone who can, be it legally or otherwise. Welcome to Remo.
Remy: A loving man who needs to keep moving. If he stops for too long, or spends too much time mulling over some drama, problem or issue, then there is a risk he'll stall and lose all artistic/creative momentum. The moral to the story here Remy: if you lose your way then just do what feels right. Don't think about it too much.
Rene: Spends a lot of money on 'stuff' and he has a large ego. Likes to wear a scarf-thing around his neck, even if it's not that cold.
Renier: Renier aspires to be some kind of mover and shaker. Mostly it's a money thing. What about love, Renier? They tell me it's the greatest moving and shaking event of all…
Reno: Reno spends far too much time in high school detention or in juvenile lock-up. Reno, some advice from up here in the box: For one month get away from those friends of yours that lead you astray, find  yourself a pass-time that involves using your body, stay off all drugs and alcohol, get some fruit, vegetables, nuts, fish and water into you, find a couple of good books to read and get to bed early. I'm telling you, one month of this will change your life. Please report back to us when you're done.
Renton: What a splendid dipstick Renton is. It’s true, he’s never mended a fence in his life and he wouldn’t know how. He couldn’t ‘carpenter’ his way out of a paper bag and as an inner-city city-slicker, perhaps we wouldn’t expect him to. Calm and quiet like a heavy, clean and empty water glass, Renton does well on eHarmony, and so he should. He’s a nice guy.
Reon: Reon rarely works with his hands. He has 40 shirts in his cupboard but only 2 of them are cleaned and ironed. What does that mean? Well, it depends on how much importance you place on clean, ironed shirts, I suppose…
Resee: A litle Malaysian guy who can't wipe the smile off his face. It's impossible not to love the guy, but don't waste his time - or ours - by expcecting him to be the head negotiator at the meeting, or deliver the bad news at the AGM. Resee is too spiritual for that crap.
Reuben: The name of a mountain stream that is cool, calm and clean. (Either that or he's in the money markets and only divulges his secrets if it means a lazy mill' is going to fall into one of his accounts, in which case not even his closest friends or partner is ever likely to find out.)
Reuven: Man, this boy can dance. So, no, he's not shy. There's a mountain being moved behind the scenes.
Reve: Reve will only sleep with a girl, or a man if he's into them, if they have clean, white linen sheets with a very high thread count.
Revell: Revell fights hard with himself not to party as hard as can be. He turns up to work on time and sometimes he even has to fight hard to do that. Best of all, Revell is trying hard to be a good man. It's even more impressive given that he finds the whole story of life filled with so much irrelevant, meaningless bullshit.
Rex:
Option A:  Maggie’s father. Also black.

Option B:  Good mates with Neville, Graeme, Bruce and Kev. (Look ‘em up.)
Rheen: With a name that’s about as exciting as a well-functioning hot-water system, Rheen is an industrious little fucker with a cheeky grin. Decisions are made quickly here and he doesn’t turn around and lament at any that didn’t play out the way he intended.
Rhen: If he didn't have to eat Rhen would sleep all day, such is how chilled-out he is.
Rhett: His name is unique in the Kingdom in that it’s the only one that sounds like a motorbike being revved, such that if you say it loudly at him there’s a chance he’ll jump, but, overall, Rhett is a cool cat who wears unusual shoes. We all have a niche to fill.
Rhyce:
Rhyce is an organised man and not prone to fits of impulsive behaviour. That's not to say he never acts on the spur of the moment but there is always some measure of contemplation. And he's not stupid. For example, if he's attending a summer-time party at a two-storey house, where there is swimming pool adjacent to the building, long before he arrives he would presume some of his less mindful friends would jump into the pool from the 2nd storey balcony. What his friends won't have done however is (A) get on the phone that afternoon and ring the party hosts, casually enquiring as to the depth of the pool at the deep end, if it has one, and (B) get on the internet afterwards and determine the depth of water required for a human of X kg to drop safely into it from the height of a 2nd storey balcony.

So, naturally, in the middle of the party, Rhyce's random leap into the pool, on the surface, looks like a sporadic, zany moment of hilarious genius. And on one level it is.
Rhys: Slippery he may be, but you want him on your team. Not the oppositions.
Rian: Where as his cousin (Ryan) is someone who will imbibe any substance he can get his hands on, Rian attempts to take a stand against the tide of either peer group or social pressure by attempting not to party himself into the ground. He needs his sleep anyway. He's got a university exam to sit in the morning.
Ricardo: “Hullooooo,” he says with a very heavy accent to a lovely young girl. “I think...tonight......you would be liking to make love with me, no?”
Riccardo: Yep. See Ricardo and cease your complaining about your extra c.
Rich:
“So, where is he? He said he was going to meet me here?”
His flatmate smiles. “Nah. You know that model he met at that party last week?”
You stand there, confused. “...Yeah?”
“Well she called by half an hour ago in her convertible. His taken off with her up to the lakes for the weekend. He said to say sorry, but that you’d understand.”
“Oh fuck! That prick!”
Rich’s flatmate smiles. “Yeah, that’s exactly what he said you’d say.”
Richard: The knight in shining armour with an ill-fitting helmet that badly impedes his vision 80% of the time. He rides a big white stallion that’s not dissimilar to that ridden by Cassandra, although his task of riding anywhere quickly is made far more difficult because the horse continually tries to throw him for its personal amusement.
Richie: Richie always has fags on him and is continually on the lookout for mischief. He’s an excellent prankster and an excellent second lieutenant.
Richo:
Plucked from obscurity, how Richo pulled it off appears to be something of a miracle. True, he worked hard behind the scenes to get himself ready but, even so, we're still amazed at how well he's done. One minute he was getting his arse whacked by a bloody big cane, next minute he's at the President's house receiving the keys to the city. 
Richo is living proof that self-belief and a healthy disrespect for the system will get you everywhere.
Rick: Mr. Restless and Mr. Almost Hyperactive.
Ricki: Ricki can be a tempestuous little shit on occasion. Generally he gets into tasks quickly, rarely sitting around to watch others get some advantage ahead of him. He's not big on missing out and he's never meditated in his life.
Ricky: Ricky feels very little pain. Does that make him something of a masochist? Maybe....
Riley: Riley has an ego that won't easily lie down and it’s something that he wrestles with constantly. He’s good looking, he’s intelligent and he’s charismatic – he knows all this – but he’s a compassionate human being as well with a generous sense of stupid fun. The total story may take years to tell.
Riordan: Riordan has never done a push-up in his life and we’d be disappointed if he started now. As a borderline academic he knows a great deal about a great many things, and he is always eager to learn more. He looks a little gruff but he’s not really. He might be a little deaf, perhaps that explains his occasionally intense glare?
Ripley:
Ah, Sigourney, if only anyone was as tough as you… 
Anyway, here in the real world Ripley is a soft-handed city boy who spends 90% of his waking life staring at some kind of electronic screen in the name of both work and play. And he’s not on his own, sadly. But, Ripley is no dill.
River: River burns it at both ends and he therefore needs to drink more water than he does.
Roarke:
An accountant? Not bloody likely. He's the sort of bloke who will arrive at the party on time, behave well and enjoy the company of others until the stroke of midnight when he will stand in the middle of the room and strip to his under-trousers before yelling, "CHECK THESE OUT!"

And yes, he's wearing a pair of boxer shorts with flashing neon lights woven into them. He found them on his last trip to Tokyo and he's been in love with them ever since. In short, Roarke is and entrepreneur and he's very happy to never die wondering.
Rob: Constant like the sunrise and the sunset, his name is heavy with the burden of reliability and normalness that he would love to shun, and very occasionally does. Basically, Rob is a good guy who will do anything for you. (Note: 18% of Rob’s use this empathy to get away with dodgy deals.)
Robbie: They say the best muso’s are all slightly unhinged. Perhaps all the best artists are? There is definitely a child-like quality here and an occasional neediness. But, dogs don’t bite him and that says a lot.
Robbo: Robbo rhymes with Righto, and to that end he is a free-thinking and unselfconscious legend. He’s one of the few people on the planet who can pick up a didge’ with little or no musical history and make it sing like it’s walking on water.
Robby: Robby had it all but lacking discipline, he realized too late that pure skill was never going to be enough. He’s not always a lost soul, although if he is then all is not lost, either, because he makes up for it by often being the life of a gathering.
Robert: Yep, so Robert might be boorish sometimes, but someone has to design the road rules with a conservative mindset. Remember, the road rules exist for the worst drivers, not the best. In that regard he has almost certainly saved your life more than once. You just never knew it.
Roberto: How can one letter add so much? Roberto's Italian/Brazilian/Mexican or Spanish ancestry has allowed him a certain freedom in that he is surrounded by music, food, women, wine and friends. (Even though he still might live with his parents, and pay off a massive gambling debt.)
Robinson: Young and clean in a sporty way, Robinson is as fresh and energetic as a daisy.
Rocci:
Rocci, stop fucking complaining about shit that doesn’t matter. 
“What do  you mean?” he cries, when accused of such a thing.
Rocket: Sure, he's explosive but only in the way of yelling at his management team about what they're doing wrong. Rocket has deeply held beliefs which is why he's so passionate about the various aspects of his life. He tries to leave nothing to chance, even though he knows great luck is a rare and often untamed beast. If you're not a believer of his vision then you're better off on a different team.
Rocko: Rocko is sweet and gentle like a playful puppy with sharp teeth, and who is all about having the most fun possible without regard to consequence.
Rocky: No shy man can pull-off a Rocky, and so it is. But he’s no buffoon. He’ll plot and scheme and organise with the best of them, and he’s rarely shy when it comes to chasing ladies, either.
Rococo: Rococo is no lawyer. Indeed, the only way he would ever wind up in the Supreme Court is if those fraud charges finally came back to haunt him.
Rod: Rod is intelligent and charismatic, and here for this moment. (He might also be sufficiently opinionated.)
Roderick: Once upon a time we coined him Humpty Dumpty, but maybe that was just to get a reaction out of him, and to remind him to keep a sense of humour. If he's called Roderick only, and not some other kind of nickname, then we advise you take the same measures as one would with Ross, except make sure your gun is in good working order. Goodluck.
Rodger: Well, it's true, like many men in the Kingdom Rodger likes playing with his todger. What can you do? Out there in the real world he bounces along like he's expecting fun and hilarity any second now, which might explain why he gets fired so often. He's always ducking over to someone else's work station to see what they're doing, or running to the window to see what car just pulled up, or even just leaning as far back in his chair as he can without toppling over, while staring up at the ceiling where he imagines that he is flying over an alien landscape. Where should we put him? Anyone?...
Rodney: Quick and clever. Liked by all. Forever the quiet and consummate actor.
Rodriguez:
Yes, it’s fair to say that the parents of any girls he dates don’t like him, but clearly that’s his job. I mean, we can understand their concern. The last time they permitted him to take out their daughter – and this was months ago, mind you – the girl’s mother sprung the couple in her daughter’s bedroom at 2am. In two swift moves, all Rodriguez had time to do was leap from the maiden’s bed to his pile of clothes, cover his erection and leap out the window.
I wonder if the girl’s mother has forgiven him?
Roel: A nice man who is a bit slower to catch on than most of the crowd. Or perhaps he just likes his own company, which is where he thinks more clearly.
Roger: Roger has long arms, is covered in dangly red hair and lives in the island jungles of, what used to be known as, Borneo. He has very expressive lips, he is highly intelligent and as a youngster he’s often seen on TV wearing human nappies. In short, Roger is a cooky, unorthodox and highly entertaining fellow. The End.
Rohan: Patient and contained, Rohan is the sort of bloke who makes an excellent professional photographer.
Rolan: A caver. He nearly died on a mountain in New Zealand once, but that hasn’t stopped him climbing – far from it. And he was the dux of his last year in high school.
Roland: Roland is a graduate of Eton College, in England. He thinks that he is an excellent cricketer and rower, even though has no shoulders, petticoat hands and no hand-eye coordination what so ever.
Rolf: Rolf is a unique and supremely charismatic lover of life. His name sounds like a big dog barking happily at its owner in order to encourage them to come and do anything, and, consequently, Rolf has been able to foster his eccentric and artistic life exactly the way he always wanted because he never fully matured.
Roly:
Roly bustles his portly frame through the door. “Blah blah blah....you wouldn’t believe what just happened to me! Hey, did you hear the one about the priest and the donkey? Anyone seen my lighter? What are you pricks up to, anyway?” etc etc
 
Even watching him is enough to make you tired.
Roman: Roman is the supremely cool, sanguine and friendly world-traveller.
Romeo: Fair suck of the sav’, Romeo! He smiles. He’s heard it all before - the jibes about his name, that is. Is he a soldier? Fuck no. Romeo runs a cafe/restaurant, puts the least number of transactions possible through the till and loves everyone. The tax department has an entire section devoted to him. Amen.
Ron:
“G’day love,” he says when he walks through the door, exhausted.  “Hi darl’,” he hears from somewhere inside the house. 

And the stars above track silently behind a brilliant blue sky, because Ron is a hard-working, honourable man.
Ronald: As Irma’s catatonic brother, on special occasions we’ll see him attached to the front of the breweries promotional wagon. After all, everyone loves a dopy Clydesdale.
Roni: Does he speak Hebrew? Does he hang out with long-beards? There are some things you can’t jest about, with Roni. If you accused him of behaving like a woman he would want to fight you, no matter how well you know him, which is bloody absurd Roni. Chill-out mate, and if you lug around any rosary beads please, get rid of them and get yourself a skateboard, or something.
Ronin: No, he hasn't rappelled down a mountain face to save the damsel in distress, but his parents named him that way, thinking one day he might. He’s actually quite chilled out and while we cant say he’s shy, his does shy away from the limelight. A good heart. Ronin.
Ronnie: Not the petty crim’ like his kindred brother (Ronny), this guy is far suaver and savvier. Sure, Ronnie breaks the rules, but not the ones that will land you in jail, and if he ever did he’s smart enough to enact them when no one is looking. Ronnie is a man for the good times with plenty of energy, and he attracts plenty of good attention. Not one to sit around idle for days on end.
Ronny: Ronny chuckles a lot and gets on with things and, 25% of the time, at least, he hides his small-scale crimes quite nicely.
Rorey: Like his cousin below, Rorey plans and thinks big. Is it his money he's playing with? Given the likelihood of success, it's probably a smart move if it isn't. And fear not, despite the bravado Rorey ain't the total fool.
Rory:
Big name. Big responsibility. You said you can hang-glide even though you’ve never done it, mate, which is fine. So, now, here you are, on the mountain side, strapped in. Are you still ready?......Yeah?.....okay, go for it!
(and a hush goes through the crowd as he leaps.......)
Rosario: Firm but kind, Rosario is the Gentle Patriarch.
Rosco: The goofy firebrand and potent rebel, although you’ll only ever see him in action when he’s really fired-up about something, which is never that often.
Ross: TAKE ALL PRECAUTION! Keep a tranquilliser gun trained on him at all times, even if he appears tame, because he might be faking it. You just never know.
Rosso: Mmmm, well no surprises here kids. Rosso is one part Ross, obviously, one part Ian, and one part Johnny. At his heart Rosso has a deep-seated desire to do genuine good in the world, despite his playful irreverence, and if he felt the need he could successfully sell biscuits to workers in a biscuit factory.
Rouke: Uncompromising and friendly, Rouke isn't a flippant personality, although he does get bored after a while. Sure, we all do from time to time, but Rouke won't wait for someone else to amuse him. Like a heavy screwdriver opening a big tin of paint, Rouke will jimmy and push and lever either a person or a situation in order to (a) find out what's going on or (b) extract some kind of unpredictable reaction in the name of entertainment.
Rove: Fast thinker. He moves from place to place, from person to person and from moment to moment so quickly that he is effectively unembarrassable.
Row: See James, except Row lacks the disguises and he doesn’t suffer from occasional mood swings.
Rowan: He ain't no grease monkey, although he might be a swinger, who knows? What he is, is cool.
Rowen: Country boy and an a rather elemental man. Rowen is interested in life and always ready to learn, and like Kenny and a few other pseudo-mysterious cats out there, most of his friends are perpetually unsure of his whereabouts. Most important, his name opens you up when you say it and therefore there are very few bad/manipulative/evil Rowens out there in the wild....we think.
Roy: Don’t be coy Roy, it’s okay to be a boy and you’ll be surprised how many of them there are.
Royce: Royce rarely walks lightly and his blood lines can be traced all the way back to grand old England, a long, long time ago. Ridiculous, silly and pointless acts of childishness are none of his business, but that's not to say he isn't a big kid at heart. As a serious blue chip invester, however, he's not prone to putting himself in a position where everything can be squandered in a flash, and regardless whether it's his dignity, his financial state or his emotional and physical well-being. You with me?
Rudolph:
Rudolph has a grand laugh and a plethora of adoring friends but it’s true - what he makes up for in humour and levity he lacks in common sense. For example, Rudolph’s idea of a personal challenge is to drive across the country in his old Roller, stark bollock naked. After all, why take any aspect of life seriously?
Indeed.
Rudy: Rudy has two possible outcomes in life. Either he grows big and dumb, real quick, and dominates the schoolyard as a bully, ending up in a highly evolved life of crime and drugs before dying by the sword (having lived by the sword), or he grows slowly under the weight of huge intellect and eventually spends his days and years in his room trying to hack into mainframe computer systems all over the world. (The latter Rudy spent his previous life as a field mouse, the former as a ship’s anchor.)
Rupert: As a child, Rupert spent a lot of time getting into trouble without accidentally killing anyone and in adulthood he has carried-on his merry way. He probably isn’t super fit, which won’t bother him too much, he makes everyone laugh (basically whenever he wants), he’s more intelligent than the next bloke and overall he’s tremendous fun.
Russ: His name is heavy and curt like a lead weight plummeting to the bottom of the ocean, and so brief and spectacularly uninformative that there was no way he was ever going to end up like that. In actual fact, Russ secretly searches more intently than most, and definitely more than you might imagine from plainly observing him. His ego doesn’t run his life and all of us are better off for it. Thanks Russ.
Russell: Russell, the love Mussel, is like an irrepressible Cocker Spaniel who refuses to sit down and who, if remotely happy, will constantly try and have sex with your leg.
Rusty: Camps. Surfs. Fishes. Eats. Thinks. Does.
Ry: In a perfect world Ry would just surf all day, every day. All the rest of his life is just filler for when the swell is missing.
Ryan: The affable tradie’ that parties so hard on the weekend he sometimes does himself damage.
Ryder: Good guy. His ego might drive his existence but he is sufficiently cluey and compassionate, and his only really negative attribute is that he is occasionally extremely lazy.
Rye: Get him outside and he’ll find his way, but don’t give him too much rope. He sometimes forgets what he’s attached to, hence he’s liable to fly away into the universe on a whim, in which case we won’t see him for yonks. Anyway, he’s fun to have around so it’s not like keeping an eye on him presents an issue.
Ryker: My god, have you ever seen anyone spend so long in front of the mirror trying to get a tiny, 1 inch lick of head hair positioned exactly right? We haven't. Ryker, some advice from up here in the commentary box: go and volunteer for the Salvation Army for a week or two, then you'll begin to understand what really matters.
Rylan: In the band he plays the electric organ and his long curly hair makes it impossible to see the tension and the passion on his face, which is a pity. The upshot of all this is that he never has as many girls after him at the post-concert party because very few people know who he is.
Ryle: Ryle is placid like an old eagle that can’t be bothered chasing after the females any more. He’s just content to sit on his perch, take in the view, admire the surrounds and generally go about his business of being sufficiently noble.
Ryot: Yeah, Ryot is a scream until he gets arrested, which is often.
